title: The reimbursement grant requires maintaining a billion USDS of borrowing at all times or it is slashed pro rata
content:
A.2.8.2.2.2.2.4 conditions the subsidy on a debt floor: "Primes, including Spark and Grove, must each maintain a minimum borrowing of 1,000,000,000 USDS from Sky at all times to remain eligible for the full monthly reimbursement grant. If the amount borrowed falls below this threshold, the reimbursement grant will be proportionately slashed. This grant will cover the difference between the borrowing Base Rate and SOFR."

The subsidy is therefore delivered as a *reimbursement* rather than a discounted rate — the Prime pays the Base Rate and is paid back the gap — and eligibility depends on a balance maintained continuously, not on average or period-end borrowing.

The incentive this creates cuts against prudence. A Prime that finds no opportunity worth funding should repay and stop paying interest; here, dropping below the floor costs it the grant proportionally, so it is rewarded for holding a billion USDS of debt regardless of whether it has anywhere good to put the proceeds. Combined with the Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation's zero floor, which removes the downside of a position earning less than its funding cost, the pressure to stay fully drawn is considerable.

Sky's side of the bargain is legible: the subsidy is buying USDS supply and deployed liquidity, and paying for an option to borrow that goes unexercised buys nothing. The floor makes the grant a payment for actual balance-sheet usage.

The control is that "at all times" is a hard test on a live figure, and A.2.8.2.2.2.2.5 keeps the door open above it — borrowing beyond a billion is available "at the prevailing Base Rate," unsubsidised. The subsidy therefore has both a floor and a ceiling, and only the first billion is concessionary.
